title: Using DuckDB with Deno
body: I'm using Deno 1.41.3. I tried importing `npm:duckdb` and creating an in-memory database, but `deno run -A index.ts` throws `Cannot find module '/Users/<user>/Library/Caches/deno/npm/registry.npmjs.org/duckdb/0.10.1/lib/binding/duckdb.node'`. Is it possible to use DuckDB with Deno?

symptoms_visible: Running `deno run -A index.ts` with `import duckdb from "npm:duckdb"` fails because `duckdb.node` cannot be found under Deno's npm cache.
N0.label: N0 native binding missing

symptoms_visible: After installing DuckDB into local `node_modules` (and running `npm install` inside `node_modules/duckdb` to actually produce `duckdb.node`), Deno finds the binding, but loading the addon still fails: on Deno 1.40.4 the run panics inside Deno while registering the native module, and after upgrading to Deno 1.43.1 it fails with `Error in native callback`.
N1.label: N1 local native addon installed

symptoms_visible: With the canary I updated to and `DENO_FUTURE=1`, I can import DuckDB and create `Database {}`, but as soon as I actually run a query it fails.
N2_x.label: N2_x initial canary execution aftermath

symptoms_visible: On the canary I updated to, the small example from the duckdb repo (`SELECT 42 AS fortytwo` against the in-memory database) still fails as soon as the query runs.

My other setup — a remote HTTPS Parquet query (`SELECT * FROM 'https://shell.duckdb.org/data/tpch/0_01/parquet/orders.parquet' LIMIT 1000;`) run inside `Deno.serve` — prints `Database {}` and the query, then dies with `zsh: segmentation fault` on `deno 1.43.1+998036b`.
N3.label: N3 query crash reproduced

symptoms_visible: After updating to the newer build, DuckDB loads and my queries return results.
N_terminal.label: terminal DuckDB working locally

solution.intent: Work around Deno's missing npm lifecycle-script support by installing DuckDB with npm, yarn, or pnpm into a project-local node_modules directory and importing the local package.
solution.concrete_example: Run `npm install duckdb`, then use `import duckdb from "duckdb"` so DuckDB's package installation can place the native `duckdb.node` binding in local `node_modules`.
solution.inference_hint: The missing `duckdb.node` file is caused by Deno not running DuckDB's npm lifecycle/postinstall step. The reporter supplied the missing-module path; identifying the unexecuted lifecycle hook was engineer analysis.

edges.comment: The initial workaround from c0 is technically necessary and does place the native addon in local node_modules, but it exposes a separate Deno N-API execution problem rather than completing DuckDB support.

solution.intent: Present the first canary containing the initial DuckDB native-addon fix as the complete answer: tell the user this build makes DuckDB work and treat a successful import plus `Database {}` construction as proof the issue is fixed.
solution.concrete_example: Run `deno upgrade --canary` to pick up the first native-addon fix and re-run the existing example; report that DuckDB now imports and `Database {}` is constructed, and treat the issue as resolved on that basis.

edges.comment: Blind semantics are narrow here: only the claim that this first canary is itself the complete fix was falsified — the reporters then showed that actual queries still failed. The two sub-actions that accompanied it, `DENO_FUTURE=1` and keeping the npm-installed local `node_modules`, are permanent parts of the accepted final recipe and are scored on e4_N3__N_terminal, so they are deliberately not required elements of this blind edge.

question_patterns: Can you run a query on that canary and paste exactly what happens — both for a small example like `SELECT 42 AS fortytwo` and for the workload you actually care about?
When the query fails, does Deno print an error or does the process die outright, and is it the same for the local in-memory query as for your remote Parquet one?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: IT WORKS! I can import DuckDB and create the database now — thanks for your patience! But... if I actually run a query, it fails; the code I ran is the example from the duckdb repo (`SELECT 42 AS fortytwo` on an in-memory database). And on my other setup I've just updated to the last canary, `deno 1.43.1+998036b`, and I still get the same `segmentation fault`: the script creates the database and then runs `SELECT * FROM 'https://shell.duckdb.org/data/tpch/0_01/parquet/orders.parquet' LIMIT 1000;` inside `Deno.serve`; the terminal shows `Database {}`, `Listening on http://localhost:8000/`, the query, then `zsh: segmentation fault  deno run --allow-all index.ts`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The minimal local `SELECT 42 AS fortytwo` query returns 42 correctly; only a remote Parquet query over HTTPS fails.
The same minimal example still fails on the same canary, and the remote-Parquet workload dies with `Abort trap` instead of `segmentation fault`.

edges.comment: Evidence from the original reporter and the second affected user is folded into one simulated user side, and the answer reports only what those two users produced on the canary: the small duckdb-repo example fails when the query runs (failure mode not stated in text — it was a screenshot), and the separate remote-Parquet-under-`Deno.serve` workload still segfaults. The maintainer's own minimal reproduction — a panic in Deno's N-API layer, explicitly contrasted with the users' segfault — is an engineer-side observation and lives on e4 (`info_inferred_by_engineer` / `inference_hint`), not in the user's mouth.

solution.intent: Use a Deno build containing PR 24101, while retaining the local npm-installed DuckDB workaround and DENO_FUTURE=1 until lifecycle-script support is available, then verify by executing a real DuckDB query.
solution.concrete_example: Install the canary containing denoland/deno#24101, or Deno 1.44.2 or later. In the affected Deno 1.x setup, use `npm install duckdb`, import `duckdb` from local `node_modules`, and run `DENO_FUTURE=1 deno run -A index.ts`. Please retest `SELECT 42 AS fortytwo` in the updated build and confirm that it returns a result.
solution.inference_hint: There are two distinct blockers. The original missing binding comes from the absent npm lifecycle/postinstall step, while the later query failure is an internal Deno N-API compatibility bug. On the maintainer's own machine the same minimal `SELECT 42 AS fortytwo` example did not segfault but panicked at `cli/napi/js_native_api.rs` with `Option::unwrap()` on a `None` value (build 1.43.1+998036b) — that panic is a maintainer-side observation, explicitly contrasted with what the users saw, and must not be attributed to them. Engineers identified the N-API bug and fixed DuckDB query execution in PR 24101; users supplied only their own observed failures (query failure on the minimal example, `segmentation fault` on the remote-Parquet workload) and the successful retest.

edges.comment: PR 24101 was reported working in canary and slated for 1.44.2. The reporter subsequently confirmed that DuckDB worked. The unrelated lifecycle-hook work remained tracked separately in PR 23558.

satisfaction_conditions: Must distinguish the two blockers: the original `duckdb.node` file is missing because the npm lifecycle/postinstall step was not run, while the later query panic or segmentation fault is a separate Deno N-API implementation bug.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the observed progression: direct `npm:duckdb` use misses the binding, local npm installation allows the addon to load, and queries still fail on the canary that fixed loading.

The working local Deno 1.x procedure must retain the project-local npm installation and `DENO_FUTURE=1`, then update to a build containing the Deno N-API execution fix (canary at the time, or the following release).
Must not present the first canary execution fix as sufficient; it loaded the database but actual queries still failed, and the remote-Parquet workload still segfaulted.
Must ask the user to execute a DuckDB query on the fixed build and only treat the issue as resolved after that verification succeeds.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable JavaScript and data-analysis developer who can use npm, edit a small TypeScript reproduction, install Deno canaries, and test native packages, but needs guidance on Deno-specific installation modes and environment variables.
persona_hint.communication_style: Friendly, appreciative, and cooperative; shares concise reproductions and screenshots, candidly admits setup mistakes, and reports whether each instructed step works.
